## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
# Weddings with no W1
PublicDF %>%
  group_by(WeddingID) %>%
  filter(!any(Role == "W2")) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  distinct(WeddingID)
```

```{r}
no_w1 <- PublicDF %>%
  group_by(WeddingID) %>%
  filter(!any(Role == "W2")) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  distinct(WeddingID) %>%
  pull(WeddingID)

PublicDF %>%
  filter(WeddingID %in% no_w1) %>%
  select(WeddingID, Citation, ID, FirstName, Surname, Role, For) %>%
  arrange(WeddingID, Role)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
```{r}
PublicDF %>%
  filter(WeddingID == "W0215") %>%
  select(WeddingID, Citation, Date, ID, FirstName, Surname, Role, For, EnslaverID)

wedding_pairs <- PublicDF %>%
  filter(Role %in% c("B", "G")) %>%
  select(WeddingID, Citation, Date, Role, ID, FirstName, Surname, EnslaverID) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Role,
              values_from = c(ID, FirstName, Surname, EnslaverID))
# Columns: ID_B, ID_G, FirstName_B, ..., EnslaverID_B, EnslaverID_G

```

```{r}
target <- wedding_pairs %>% filter(WeddingID == "W0215")

# Both enslavers match
wedding_pairs %>%
  filter(WeddingID != "W0215",
         EnslaverID_B == target$EnslaverID_B,
         EnslaverID_G == target$EnslaverID_G)

# Either enslaver matches (looser, since the groom's identity is in doubt)
wedding_pairs %>%
  filter(WeddingID != "W0215",
         EnslaverID_B == target$EnslaverID_B | EnslaverID_G == target$EnslaverID_G)

```

```{r}
# Every row for the bride, wherever she appears
FullDF %>% filter(ID == "P0450") %>%
  select(WeddingID, Citation, Date, ID, FirstName, Surname, Role, For, EnslaverID)

# Confirm the second wedding's ID
FullDF %>% filter(Citation %in% c("088_003", "088_03")) %>% distinct(WeddingID, Citation)
FullDF %>% filter(grepl("Cruz", Surname), grepl("Diego|Juan|Julio", FirstName)) %>%
  select(WeddingID, Citation, ID, FirstName, Surname, Role)
```

```{r}
# 1. Look at both weddings first
FullDF %>% filter(WeddingID %in% c("W0101", "W0215")) %>%
  select(WeddingID, Citation, Date, ID, FirstName, Surname, Role, For, EnslaverID) %>%
  arrange(WeddingID, Role)

# 2. Pull the IDs we need
w3_id        <- FullDF$ID[FullDF$WeddingID == "W0215" & grepl("^W", FullDF$Role)]
groom_retire <- FullDF$ID[FullDF$WeddingID == "W0215" & FullDF$Role == "G"]
groom_keep   <- FullDF$ID[FullDF$WeddingID == "W0101" & FullDF$Role == "G"]
w3_id; groom_retire; groom_keep      # each should be exactly one ID

# 3. Does the retired groom ID appear in any other wedding?
FullDF %>% filter(ID == groom_retire) %>% distinct(WeddingID, Role)

```

```{r}
OldDF <- read_csv("Marriage_DF_07_15_2026.csv", col_types = cols(.default = "c"))

OldDF %>% filter(WeddingID %in% c("W0101", "W0215")) %>%
  select(WeddingID, Citation, Date, ID, firstname, lastname, Role, For, EnslaverID) %>%
  arrange(WeddingID, Role)

```

```{r}
# Look first, using the old file's column names
OldDF %>% filter(WeddingID %in% c("W0101", "W0215")) %>%
  select(WeddingID, Citation, Date, ID, firstname, lastname, Role, For, EnslaverID) %>%
  arrange(WeddingID, Role)

OldDF <- OldDF %>%
  # 1. Antonio (P0107): move to W0101 as W3 (keeps his own Citation and Date)
  mutate(Role      = if_else(WeddingID == "W0215" & ID == "P0107", "W3", Role),
         WeddingID = if_else(WeddingID == "W0215" & ID == "P0107", "W0101", WeddingID)) %>%
  # 2. Delete the remaining W0215 rows (Francisca's second bride row and the second groom)
  filter(WeddingID != "W0215") %>%
  # 3. Julio becomes Diego (the W0101 groom)
  mutate(firstname = if_else(WeddingID == "W0101" & Role == "G", "Diego", firstname))
```

```{r}
n_distinct(OldDF$WeddingID)                            # one lower than before
sum(OldDF$ID == "P0450")                               # 1
OldDF %>% filter(WeddingID == "W0101") %>% arrange(Role)   # B, G, W1, W2, W3

```

```{r}
write_csv(OldDF, "Marriage_DF_10_12_2026.csv")
```

```{r}
# 1. Look first
FullDF %>% filter(WeddingID %in% c("W0101", "W0215")) %>%
  select(WeddingID, Citation, Date, ID, FirstName, Surname, Role, For, EnslaverID) %>%
  arrange(WeddingID, Role)

# 2. Compare the two groom rows before deleting anything
FullDF %>% filter(WeddingID %in% c("W0101", "W0215"), Role == "G") %>%
  select(WeddingID, ID, FirstName, Surname, Race, Status, EnslaverName, EnslaverID)

```

```{r}
# 3. The fix
FullDF <- FullDF %>%
  # Antonio (P0107): move to W0101 as W3 (keeps his own Citation and Date)
  mutate(Role      = if_else(WeddingID == "W0215" & ID == "P0107", "W3", Role),
         WeddingID = if_else(WeddingID == "W0215" & ID == "P0107", "W0101", WeddingID)) %>%
  # Delete the remaining W0215 rows (Francisca's second bride row and the second groom)
  filter(WeddingID != "W0215") %>%
  # Julio becomes Diego, and the 010_015 typo is corrected on the original four rows
  mutate(FirstName = if_else(WeddingID == "W0101" & Role == "G", "Diego", FirstName),
         Citation  = if_else(WeddingID == "W0101" & Role %in% c("B", "G", "W1", "W2"),
                             "010_150", Citation))

# 2. Compare the two groom rows before deleting anything
#FullDF %>% filter(WeddingID %in% c("W0101", "W0215"), Role == "G") %>%
  #select(WeddingID, ID, FirstName, Surname, Race, Status, EnslaverName, EnslaverID)
```
